prompt: A particle's velocity is $v(t) = 3t^2 - 12$ meters per second. Find its acceleration at $t = 2$ seconds, in meters per second squared.
hint: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: $a(t) = v'(t)$.

hints.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: $a(t) = v'(t)$.

explanation: Note $v(2) = 12 - 12 = 0$: the particle is momentarily stopped at $t = 2$ but accelerating hard, so it immediately starts moving in the positive direction.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rate of change of velocity
steps: Average acceleration over that tenth of a second: $\frac{1.23}{0.1} = 12.3$ m/s$^2$.
Close to the instantaneous $12$ m/s$^2$; shrinking the window would bring it closer still.
